decision.title: The codegen chapter builds a tree of the TypeScript program and prints it with XSLT (packet book-4)
decision.summary: The codegen chapter builds an abstract tree of the TypeScript program with XQuery, prints it with one XSLT template rule per element, and checks the printed files by parsing them with sxml:parse-code.

body.p: , after , , , . The owner: for the codegen examples, a tree of the TypeScript code translated with XSLT is easier to follow in the book than endless string concatenation.

item.p: Pipeline. api.xml and library.xsd go through program.xq (XQuery, the library module typescript.xqm) to a program tree, generated/program.xml, then through print.xsl (XSLT) to types.ts, client.ts and server.ts, one xsl:result-document per module; openapi.xsl is unchanged. generate.xq (fn:put of string-constructor text) is gone; generate.sh runs validate, the query with --output, the printer with --result-directory, and the OpenAPI stylesheet.

Vocabulary: our own, not tree-sitter's. sxml:parse-code's tree is concrete (every token and space; its string value is the source), so writing one means writing the text anyway. The generator writes an abstract tree in no namespace, named after TypeScript's words: module, comment, doc, import, type-alias, interface, property, method, function, parameter, returns, body, type, array-type, union, predicate, statement, const, return, if/then/else, for-of, name, string, number, boolean, regex, call (function or method of the first child), member, not, binary (named operators, n-ary), await, array, object/entry, arrow. Names are attributes, parts children; a string holds its text, not a literal. tree-sitter's names are used where code is read: the round-trip check.

Printer. One template rule per element; layout in one place: an indentation function counting enclosing blocks, a priority-1 rule for every line that wraps xsl:next-match, a priority-2 rule for empty lines, a print:braces function (one-statement then without else stays on the if's line). No parentheses rules: the generator never nests binary expressions (said in the text). An unknown element is an error. braces.xsl imports it and overrides $indent and print:braces: the same tree in a second style.

Imports are computed from the tree (ts:module): names the types module declares come from ./types.ts (type-only for types), called functions declared nowhere from ../runtime.ts. The unused checkDecimal import is gone as a result.

Round trip. check.xq parses the printed files with sxml:parse-code (typescript) and raises local:mismatch when a client function lacks an Implementation method or a createHandler route, a runtime import is not exported by runtime.ts, or the client lacks a function of the tree.

String constructors stay only as the one-line contrast at the start of the section, where the text says they are the simplest tool for a line or two; the book's glossary entry says the same, and gains "Printer" and "Syntax tree".

Sections. codegen-typescript.md ("Building a Tree of the Program with XQuery"), new codegen-printer.md ("Printing the Tree with XSLT"), codegen-running.md unchanged, codegen-pipeline.md gains "Checking the generated code". The generated TypeScript changed only in its header comment, the dropped import, brace-less one-statement ifs and one folded concatenation.

Verified: check-book-examples.sh on a release build of a HEAD snapshot: the five codegen files, 46 examples, all match (the Node section with SXML_JAVASCRIPT set to an empty directory, since it imports no package; the package was not built); tsc --strict (6.0.2, @types/node) on demo.ts and the generated files, in both styles and for library-2.xsd; mdbook build. No library bug found.
